items.title: pg_ivm 1.17 released
items.summary: IVM Development Group is pleased to announce the release of pg_ivm 1.17.Changes since the v1.16 release include:What's ChangedNew featuresAdd replace option to restore_immv() (Yugo Nagata)Allow restore_immv() to replace existing IMMV metadata entries. Add a --pg-upgrade option to pg_ivm_dump_metadata to generate restore commands that can be used with pg_upgrade. Previously, restoring IMMVs after pg_upgrade failed because old IMMV entries remained in pg_ivm_immv.Bug fixesFix incorrect ispopulated state after restore_immv() (Gori)restore_immv() incorrectly left ispopulated = false after restoring an IMMV. As a result, a later refresh_immv() could add a duplicate set of IVM triggers, causing incorrect view maintenance.Improve unique key derivation for automatic index creation (Yugo Nagata)Derive unique keys from the original view definition instead of the rewritten query. This enables automatic index creation for queries where uniqueness can be determined from the original query shape, such as queries containing EXISTS clauses.Also reject target lists containing set-returning functions, since such queries cannot have a unique key even when all primary key columns are present. In addition, ignore subqueries without range table entries, since they produce at most one row when they do not contain set-returning functions.Replace the DETAIL message reported when automatic index creation fails with a more general description, since the reasons preventing unique-key derivation can be complex.Fix crash during index creation with LATERAL subqueries (Yugo Nagata)Fix assertion failure in check_immv_compatibility() (Yugo Nagata)About pg_ivmpg_ivm is an extension module that provides Incremental View Maintenance (IVM) feature.Incremental View Maintenance (IVM) is a way to make materialized views up-to-date inwhich only incremental changes are computed and applied on views rather than recomputing.pg_ivm provides a kind of immediate maintenance, in which materialized views are updatedimmediately after a base table is modified.Source repository: https://github.com/sraoss/pg_ivm

items.title: HypoPG 1.4.4 is out!
items.summary: HypoPG 1.4.4 is out!Tainan, Taiwan - Sun 25 Oct 2026HypoPG 1.4.4I'm pleased to announce the release of the version 1.4.4 of HypoPG, anextension adding support for Hypothetical Indexes, compatible with PostgreSQL9.2 and above.ChangelogBug fixes:Fix hypothetical index name for Oid >= 2^31 (Devrim Gündüz)Fix memory leak of WITH clause options (Devrim Gündüz)Check maximum number of columns with included columns too (Devrim Gündüz,  Julien Rouhaud)Invalidate hypothetical indexes when receiving an invalidation message for  on the dependent object when possible (relations, functions, access  methods, operator classes, types), or just any invalidation message for all  other object type (Julien Rouhaud, per initial from Devrim Gündüz)Fix indcollation and indclass columns in hypopg() (Matt Blewitt)Prevent failed EXPLAIN from affecting later queries (Matt Blewitt, Julien  Rouhaud)Protect hypothetocal Oid range query against user objects (Julien Rouhaud,  per report from Matt Blewitt)Miscellaneous:Additional pg 19 compatibility fixes (Julien Rouhaud, with one problem  reported by Nacho Alonso Portillo)Links & CreditsThank to the users who reported bugs, they are all cited in the CHANGELOG file.HypoPG is an open project. Any contribution to build a better tool is welcome.You just have to send your ideas, features requests or patches using the githubrepository at github.com/HypoPG/hypopg.LinksDownload: github.com/HypoPG/hypopg/releasesBug tracker: github.com/HypoPG/hypopg/issues

items.title: pg_hdr_histogram 1.0.0 - exact percentiles in PostgreSQL
items.summary: pg_hdr_histogram is a PostgreSQL extension for exact-latency percentiles.Most monitoring tools approximate percentiles from fixed buckets. pg_hdr_histogramstores a full HDR histogram as a first-class type, so p50 / p99 / p99.9 aremeasurements (~0.1% relative precision over 6 orders of magnitude), not estimates —and histograms merge losslessly across time windows and hosts.Built on HdrHistogram_c.Aggregates hdr_add and hdr_merge, parallel-safe, trusted = true.Author: Vladimir Pavliv.Source: https://github.com/vovcke/pg_hdr_histogram
